rules: Verified project initialization path: create_project persists the project record only. For multiple already-specified task records in that project, parse_prd can persist them in one native call using the returned projectId. It is a pattern-based record importer, not intelligent task design. Use it only when its input restrictions preserve the complete intended work and required fields; ordinary create_task remains available for records that do not fit.

The verified lossless input form is blank-line-separated ASCII paragraphs, each at most 500 characters: one first line "- TITLE" with a plain title longer than five characters, followed by "Details: ..." lines containing the full record details. No other line may start a task pattern. Do not shorten away requirements to fit; use ordinary task creation instead. Keep estimateComplexity=true for the verified path, but its keyword-based estimates are not proof of real difficulty. Imported priority/status defaults and heuristic tags/estimates may need legitimate corrections if requirements differ.

parse_prd writes flat records: generateSubtasks does not create a hierarchy, and dependencies are not inferred. Its receipt omits created IDs. Retrieve actual IDs with list_tasks using the same projectId, showHierarchy=false, includeCompleted=true and parentId omitted; then use ordinary update_task with those IDs for any required parent/dependency links. Inspect persisted contents and relationships. Repeating the import duplicates records, and source does not promise a transaction; inspect saved state after an error before deciding what remains. Never treat imported heuristics or a successful receipt as completed external work.
